sections.normalized_html:
We are given a right triangle with a right angle at point [MATH: D,] and we are asked to find [MATH: \sin E.]

By definition, the sine of an angle in a right triangle is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the hypotenuse. In this triangle:

  • Angle [MATH: E] is at vertex [MATH: E.]

  • The side opposite angle [MATH: E] is [MATH: \overline{DF},] which has length [MATH: 8.]

  • The hypotenuse is [MATH: \overline{EF},] which has length [MATH: 17.]

So, [MATH: \sin E = \dfrac{8}{17}.]
